citations.review_text: I mean theres not enough words to express my appreciation for this game. Its a masterpiece, atleast for me. I remember first watching Radbrads walkthrough of this game way back in 2016 on youtube and I instantly fell in love with the characters, the story and the environment. The remaster does justice to the original in every aspect as far as graphics is concerned. The characters appear way more realistic in the remastered version and their facial expressions are also remarkable, to say the least. The story is amazing and the way Joel grows closer to Ellie and overcomes his guilt over losing his loved ones was portrayed beautifully. Its sad that in today's era you dont get to see a lot of games with as much depth as this game has. I highly recommend trying it out. A few things though, the game is demanding as hell in terms of hardware and that fact must be kept in mind while buying it. There are a few areas where I had to reload the checkpoint cause Ellie wont get on the board. Apart from that there was no issue. The game ran flawlessly.

This port is okay. It did experience crashes at first but it eventually became smooth to play. You'll want a 16GB vRam card for this to handle loading, otherwise you could be interrupted in the middle of an encounter.

This is worth playing to play Part 2. I found Part 2 more entertaining to play.

​The Last of Us Part I is the definitive way to experience one of the greatest video game narratives ever told. Following Joel and Ellie’s bleak, grueling journey across a ruined America is just as emotionally devastating and gripping today as it was years ago. The complete graphical overhaul breathes incredible new life into the world, making the characters' expressions and the decaying environments feel hauntingly real.
​🟢 Pros
​Unrivaled Storytelling: A deeply moving, cinematic narrative with phenomenal performances, unmatched character development, and incredible emotional weight.
​Stunning Next-Gen Visuals: Built from the ground up for modern hardware, featuring breathtaking lighting, highly detailed character models, and hyper-realistic facial animations.
​Tense and Brutal Combat: The stealth and combat mechanics feel incredibly heavy, visceral, and intense, where every bullet and crafted item matters for survival.
​Excellent Audio Design: The hauntingly beautiful acoustic soundtrack by Gustavo Santaolalla, combined with terrifyingly immersive sound effects (like the Clickers), creates an unmatched atmosphere.
​🔴 Cons
​Heavy Hardware Demands: The game is extremely resource-intensive, requiring a powerful PC and a substantial amount of VRAM to run smoothly at high settings.
​Linear Gameplay: While the story is unmatched, the core gameplay loop (stealth, shoot, move ladders/pallets) is strictly linear and doesn't offer much room for open exploration.
​Shaders Compilation: On the first launch (or after GPU driver updates), waiting for the shaders to build can take a frustratingly long time before you can actually play.
​Final Verdict: 9.5/10
​Highly Recommended. Despite being a heavy game to run on PC, it is an absolute masterpiece of interactive storytelling. If your hardware can handle it, this is a gaming experience that everyone should witness at least once.

citations.review_text: The original game is good. The expansion is poor and boring. The repetitive nature of the enemies after the mid-game also gets really boring.
Good characters but repetitive gameplay and level design

The Last of Us Part I is a third-person action-adventure game where you guide Joel and Ellie across a post-apocalyptic America after a fungal outbreak has changed what is left of the world. It mixes stealth, combat, scavenging, crafting, and story-focused exploration while following their relationship as they move through abandoned cities, settlements, and infected territory. This version is a remake of the original game with updated visuals, revised combat and exploration, expanded accessibility options, and the Left Behind expansion included.

Pros
✔️ An amazing story about found family - Joel and Ellie’s relationship is the heart of the game, and watching that bond form through survival is still what makes it hit so hard.
✔️ Strong themes handled with care - It asks a lot of questions about morality, protection, grief, and what people become when survival is the only thing left. The world is unrealistic, but the choices people make in it feel painfully believable.
✔️ Gameplay still holds up well - The mix of stealth, scavenging, crafting, and combat gives it a lot of replayability. You can approach encounters in different ways, which helps the game stay fun even when you know the story.

Cons
❌ Companion AI can pull you out of it - When Ellie or another companion runs straight through danger and enemies magically ignore them, it can break the tension for a second.
❌ Some middle sections drag - There are parts in the middle that could have been tightened up a bit without losing the story.
❌ Resource gathering feels a little dated now - At the time, the scavenging and crafting systems stood out a lot more. Playing now, I found myself either overstocked and not using much, or completely missing the thing I needed when it mattered.

Conclusion
This game is a masterpiece, and I think it is hard to argue against that. The story still lands, the world is still easy to get pulled into, and the relationship between Joel and Ellie carries so much of what makes it work. As …

On top of the superb voice acting and story the action is fun and intense too. You better have your guns ready and inventory figured out because you are constantly switching weapons , conserving ammo or stealth killing. The maps are pretty stream lined but the scenery is equally pretty and fun to look at. I have saved a few screenshots. Do you not miss this game!

claims.claim: The PC version suffers from performance instability, including frame drops and stutters during gameplay regardless of settings changes.

citations.review_text: I love the game but this version runs like DOO DOO on my PC... I wish they optimised it more or let us play the 2014 remaster instead...

incredible game, the combat with ammo management, tight controls, backpack for weapons, are all really fun. the difficulty changes that are in the game are the best kind, that aren't just higher enemy health and damage, its instead detection time, aggression, enemy intelligence etc. only complaint is that the game seems to he highly unstable, even though my laptop specs should be able to run this on medium at a solid 60 or at least low at stable 60. but regardless of settings changes high or low, there are always large frame drops and stutters. not sure what's up with this PC port of the game, but i simply resorted to capping it at 40 and keeping the rest of the settings high since its going to stutter and lag regardless. game itself is still great.

In my opinion, The Last of Us is one of the greatest video games ever made. Especially when it comes to storytelling. It delivers an incredibly emotional journey that pulls you in from beginning to end and keeps you invested in every moment.

What makes this game so special is the relationship between Joel and Ellie. Their story is beautifully written. They start off as complete strangers who barely trust each other, but as the journey unfolds, you can slowly see their bond grow stronger. That development feels natural, making every conversation and every difficult moment hit even harder. Over time, Joel begins to see Ellie as far more than just the girl he's been tasked to protect. After losing Sarah twenty years earlier, Ellie gives him a reason to care again and, ultimately, a new purpose in life.

The gameplay is so much fun! The remake is absolutely gorgeous. The visuals are stunning, the environments are incredibly detailed, and the atmosphere is second to none. Whether you're exploring abandoned cities, sneaking past infected, fighting the worst thing in the postapocalyptic world -> PEOPLE, the game constantly keeps you immersed in its world.

My only real criticism is the PC version. Unfortunately, it's really badly optimized... Even with powerful hardware, you'll occasionally encounter frame rate drops and brief stutters that can briefly interrupt the experience. Thankfully, these issues never overshadowed what is otherwise an exceptional remake.

I completed the game 100% on Grounded difficulty, and it was an unforgettable experience. It was challenging, emotional, and rewarding from start to finish. It's definitely a game I'll return to someday, if only for the nostalgia of experiencing Joel and Ellie's journey again.

An absolute masterpiece! 10/10

citations.review_text: Good story and art. Don't expect the controls to be smooth in combat or puzzles to work smoothly. Once the game has downloaded you may need to wait up to a few hours for the shader compilation process to complete. This is disappointing, but necessary. Runs very slowly on older 4Gb graphics cards, use 16Gb RX/RTX cards for best results.

It's one of the best games ever made, truly. The story, the characters, the world - its just like a brilliant movie. What Naughty Dog and Niel Drunkman did to this game's story in the second part should be considered a crime. My only complaint would be shader rendering which takes AGES in this game.
Great story, good graphics. Only downside is the pre-caching of shaders which takes quite some time after every update of the game client.
